featured_reviews.name: ashok mukherjee
featured_reviews.review_text:
Happy experience...
Thanks doctors....

Yes my friends,
People write many nasty experience they face in hospital or with doctors. Very few write their sweet experiences in hospital or with doctors.

So I thought to share my excellent sweet experience with a small, faraway hospital but with exceptional expertise in the field of knee replacement and other orthopedic and neurological complication.

My wife Operated for knee replacement on 15th...At 11 in the morning (to 2.30 pm) including recovery time inside operation theatre...

Then shifted to ICU.
Operation was good, my wife was in jolly mood and smiling while coming out from OT after the replacement ... But after 2 hrs of shifting to ICU, the real pain started... Wife was crying like mad for pain... But through medication by 8 pm it has started reducing... and she slept.
Nxt day, 16th, morning no pain...and shifted to pvt room cabin. I also staying in the same room with her. Excellent clean cosy room with all necessary requirements like AC, TV, eye catching view from 4th floor Window, attached very clean bath (no balcony), clean and daily fresh linen.

17th.. Sr Doctors and physiotherapist started her to walk and bent the new knee to 90°...

This was regular exercise, bending knee to 90° and walking in the corridor with the help of walker and physiotherapist till 19th...

And on 19th all bandage and all drain-pipes ( 3 in total... For Blood to drain our excess blood at operated knee, one for urine, one at spinal joint to push different medicine ) removed and....
discharged in the afternoon by doctor...
Same day, 19th, came to home by evening.

She is recovering nicely.... Walking inside the flat with the help of walker... pain she feel very very rarely.

After 9th day from operation, today (24th March) was the first check up...and it is absolutely OK.
Infact, my wife walk through out the day in hospital alone with the help of walker.
Today, she has been allowed by doctor to move and do morning/evening walk with walker and asked for further check up after 15 days.
No medicine given except multivitamin for further recovery as she has no pain.

We are very very happy for the excellent smooth operation, expertise of doctors, quick recovery process with effective treatment, support of Jr. Doctors, Physiotherapist, Metron, Sisters, Brothers, room boy and aayas for 24×7 and overall management of the hospital.

Well behaved people....
No extra billing...

We, and no one, before surgery, expected that after operation on 2nd day pain would vanish... she would walk and bend knee to 90°and get discharge on 4th day...!!!

All credit goes to Dr. Rahul Bade and his team including Anesthesists Dr. Ganesh Kolhe at Sparsh Multi-Speciality Hospital.

Thank you...well done, doctor !!!
🙏🙏🙏

Thanks to Lt. Col Dr Amogh Yadav from Mumbai and Dr. Rahul Mane for strongly recomanding us the hospital.

(Note : Treatment was going on at Sanchiti Hospital. But operated at Sparsh Multi Speciality Hospital)

customer_updates.name: Explorewithrohitmaurya
customer_updates.text:
The Malabar Hill Elevated Nature Trail offers a calm and well-managed experience, especially for those looking for a quiet break from Mumbai’s chaos.
The entry and exit process is smooth, well-organized, and handled professionally. The security staff deserve special mention—they’re polite, helpful, and clearly serious about their responsibility, which adds to a feeling of safety and discipline.
The walkway itself is quite small, and this is where expectations need to be realistic. While many trees and birds are tagged with names, actual wildlife sightings are limited. During my walk, I only spotted Indian parrots and crows—interestingly, two types of crows: one completely black and another with a grey neck, the kind commonly seen across the country.
The environment is quiet and peaceful, and you do feel good walking there. However, it is not very dense or forest-like, which was a disappointment for me. If you’re expecting a rich, immersive nature trail, this may feel underwhelming. The short length of the walkway further adds to that feeling—it ends just when you start settling into the experience.
Overall:
A neatly maintained, calm space with good management and discipline. Best suited for a short, relaxed walk and first-time visitors. Don’t expect dense greenery or a long trail—think of it as a brief nature pause rather than a full escape into the wild.

featured_reviews.name: Pratik B.
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited the Malabar Elevated Nature Trail yesterday and it turned out to be a beautifully planned and refreshing experience. It offers a completely different perspective of Mumbai compared to the usual views from Nariman Point or Marine Lines. This side feels quieter, greener, and far more immersive.

I had booked the 6 am to 7 am slot to catch the sunrise, and it was absolutely worth it. Around 6:13 am, the trail slowly transitioned from darkness to soft morning light and then into a warm sunlit path. Watching that gradual change while surrounded by greenery made the experience feel very special. Even in peak summer, the trail remains surprisingly lush.

At that hour, the environment is calm and soothing. You can hear birds chirping, feel the gentle sea breeze, and enjoy a peaceful start to the day before the city gets busy. The weather is generally pleasant early on, though a bit of humidity is possible depending on the day.

One thoughtful aspect of the trail is the informative signage placed along the way. There are well designed metal information panels that describe the trees, plants, birds, insects, and small wildlife you might come across, with details provided in both Marathi and English. It adds an educational layer to the walk and helps you connect more deeply with the surroundings.

A few things to keep in mind. Entry is strictly through pre booked tickets, so it is best to book a few days in advance as there is no on the spot booking. There is no parking available, so public transport is the way to go. Your ticket is required for both entry and exit, so keep it handy and make sure your phone is charged.

Visitor numbers are limited to around 200 people per slot, which helps maintain the peace and cleanliness of the space. The trail is currently very well maintained, and it would be great if everyone continues to respect that.

It feels like a thoughtful initiative inspired by places like Singapore, and credit to BMC for creating something like this in the city. Hopefully, more such spaces come up across Mumbai.

Overall, this is a must visit if you enjoy nature, calm surroundings, and unique views of the city.
